items.title: Demo-account trading has never executed
items.detail: The brief asks for trades executed on the Kalshi demo account. No demo API key exists in this environment and one cannot be self-provisioned: a demo account is created by a person at demo.kalshi.co and the private key is downloadable only once. collector/live_trading.py is implemented, self-tested, refuses to run without credentials, and is wired into the pipeline via KALSHI_DEMO_API_KEY_ID / KALSHI_DEMO_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH secrets.
items.impact: Portfolio numbers on the site are simulated, not demo-account results.

items.title: A simulated-trading bug was found on live data and is archived, not erased
items.detail: The complement-arbitrage rule was first written backwards: it required YES bid + NO bid to be BELOW 1.00 before buying both sides, but buying YES and NO costs 2 - (YES bid + NO bid) and pays $1, so the edge only exists when the bids sum ABOVE 1.00. The buggy version lost $449.84 across 26 closed simulated trades in the first two live runs. The rule now requires YES bid + NO bid >= 1 + 0.03, both legs must price inside $0.02-$0.98, and two regression tests pin the behaviour. The pre-fix ledger is kept in data/paper/archive/ledger-2026-11-20-pre-arbitrage-fix.json as the audit trail; the live ledger was reset so the portfolio page reflects the corrected engine only.
items.impact: Portfolio figures before 2026-11-20 13:40Z are not comparable with later figures.

items.title: Resolved markets report status 'finalized', not only 'settled'
items.detail: The first resolutions tracker only counted status == 'settled' and therefore reported zero resolved markets while four markets already carried a result. Verified against GET /markets/KX10SONG-26-KAR, which returned status 'finalized' together with result 'yes', settlement_value_dollars '1.0000' and a settlement_ts. The tracker now accepts both states and records the settlement value, timestamp and raw status as evidence.
items.impact: Early resolution counts understated outcomes; fixed and re-verified.

items.title: Jump detection compares two of our own observations, not exchange trades
items.detail: A move is flagged when two consecutive collector observations differ by >= $0.10 in the mid price. If a price moves and reverts between two runs the move is not recorded, and a slow drift of 5c twice is not flagged even though it totals 10c. Exchange candles are backfilled where available but are not used for jump detection because they can lag live quotes by a few seconds.
items.impact: The sharp-move log is a lower bound on real volatility.

items.title: Live push (WebSocket) not enabled
items.detail: Kalshi's WebSocket requires an authenticated handshake even for public market-data channels, so a signature needs credentials. The site polls REST every 15 minutes instead. This is a documented API constraint, not an omission.
items.impact: Updates are as fresh as the last pipeline run (timestamp shown on every page).

items.title: Causes of ≥ $0.10 moves are unattributed
items.detail: Moves are detected from exchange prices. Naming a news cause would be a claim needing a source, so every move is labelled unverified until a reviewer files a source URL in data/attributions.json.
items.impact: The sharp-move page shows facts and links, not explanations.

items.title: One editorial rule in the gas topic
items.detail: Gas-price membership requires a Kalshi 'Oil and energy' / 'Oil & Gas' tag AND the word 'gas' in the series title. Without the title test, oil-inventory series would be counted as gasoline price markets. This is the only editorial test in the topic config and it is declared here rather than hidden in code.
items.impact: Possibly excludes a gas series whose title omits the word 'gas'.

items.title: Kalshi's Culture category is nearly empty
items.detail: The live API returns only two series under category=Culture, so this dashboard defines Culture as Culture + Entertainment + Social. Awards, music, TV and movie markets live under Entertainment; the mapping is shown on each page that uses it.
items.impact: Culture numbers are broader than the literal category name.

items.title: Demo market data is not representative
items.detail: Kalshi states demo markets 'may not be reflective of those in real markets'. A probe of the demo endpoint returned 200 open markets of which 193 were multivariate combination markets with zero volume. Live prices therefore come from the public production read endpoint; the demo environment is reserved for order execution.
items.impact: Rankings reflect production markets, while executions target demo markets.

items.title: No single 'total money at stake' figure exists
items.detail: Kalshi's public API exposes per-market volume and open interest, not a committed capital pool. The dashboard reports traded dollar volume, open-interest dollars and resting liquidity instead, and never presents a made-up aggregate.
items.impact: Rankings use traded dollars, which can differ from capital currently at risk.

items.title: Per-series fee multipliers are only partly transcribed
items.detail: Kalshi's fee schedule lists per-series multipliers in a table whose PDF text layer is partly garbled. Only rows that could be read unambiguously are encoded; all other series use the schedule defaults (taker M=1, maker M=0). Series with a non-standard multiplier outside that subset would be fee-mispriced in simulation.
items.impact: Simulated fees may differ from exchange fees for unusual series.

items.title: Price history begins with the first collector run
items.detail: Chart series are built from observations this repo has collected. They are not exchange history and are not back-filled; the candlestick endpoint is used only where a real exchange history exists for the requested window.
items.impact: Charts get richer over time; early windows can be sparse.

items.detail: Last preflight: KALSHI_DEMO_API_KEY_ID is not set; KALSHI_DEMO_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH is not set
